column5: Harmonisation: This dataset merges and harmonises records previously distributed across Major-Dataset.csv subsets (formerly 1.1, 3.1 and 6.1). It contains the most complete set of identifiers and variables required for epidemiological analyses (e.g., health zone/health area, and where available age/sex and village). Use this dataset as the primary source for comparative analyses between skin-snip microscopy and anti-Ov16. Recommended use: HA/HZ-level analyses; comparisons of skin-snip and Ov16; most descriptive epidemiology. For GIS mapping, use Dataset 2.1 (clean spatial join keys; fewer missing geocoding fields). Dataset 2.1 includes fewer tested individuals than 1.1 (e.g., 66/173 skin-snip positive in 2.1 vs 74/203 in 1.1). Dataset 2.2 provides additional age/sex information in some strata and contains 2015 REMO observations for individuals not tested by skin snip or Ov16. Dataset 2.2 contains no Ov16, so it cannot be used for Ov16–skin-snip concordance analyses.

column5: Harmonisation: This dataset merges and harmonises records previously distributed across Major-Dataset.csv subsets (formerly 1.1, 3.1 and 6.1). It contains the most complete set of identifiers and variables required for epidemiological analyses (e.g., health zone/health area, and where available age/sex and village). Use this dataset as the primary source for comparative analyses between skin-snip microscopy and anti-Ov16. Recommended use: HA/HZ-level analyses; comparisons of skin-snip and Ov16; most descriptive epidemiology. For GIS mapping, use Dataset 2.1 (clean spatial join keys; fewer missing geocoding fields). Dataset 2.1 includes fewer tested individuals than 1.1 (e.g., 66/173 skin-snip positive in 2.1 vs 74/203 in 1.1). Dataset 2.2 provides additional age/sex information in some strata and contains 2015 REMO observations for individuals not tested by skin snip or Ov16. Dataset 2.2 contains no Ov16, so it cannot be used for Ov16–skin-snip concordance analyses.

Relationship to Dataset 1.1: Dataset 1.1 is a harmonised analytic dataset that includes anti-Ov16 results (enabling test comparisons) and applies stricter inclusion/exclusion of certain villages/records. Dataset 2.1 retains a broader set of REMO/skin-snip records for spatial representation and includes CDTI coverage information for Rethy sourced from the MDA coverage dataset (2014–2015).

Recommended use: GIS/spatial summaries; REMO context combined with skin-snip microscopy.

column5:
Contains REMO classifications and skin-snip results aligned to health areas/health zones for mapping and spatial summaries. Skin-snip data overlap with Dataset 1.1 but with differences in inclusion criteria and geographic coverage.

Relationship to Dataset 1.1: Dataset 1.1 is a harmonised analytic dataset that includes anti-Ov16 results (enabling test comparisons) and applies stricter inclusion/exclusion of certain villages/records. Dataset 2.1 retains a broader set of REMO/skin-snip records for spatial representation and includes CDTI coverage information for Rethy sourced from the MDA coverage dataset (2014–2015).

Recommended use: GIS/spatial summaries; REMO context combined with skin-snip microscopy.

column5:
Contains REMO classifications and skin-snip results aligned to health areas/health zones for mapping and spatial summaries. Skin-snip data overlap with Dataset 1.1 but with differences in inclusion criteria and geographic coverage.

Relationship to Dataset 1.1: Dataset 1.1 is a harmonised analytic dataset that includes anti-Ov16 results (enabling test comparisons) and applies stricter inclusion/exclusion of certain villages/records. Dataset 2.1 retains a broader set of REMO/skin-snip records for spatial representation and includes CDTI coverage information for Rethy sourced from the MDA coverage dataset (2014–2015).

Recommended use: GIS/spatial summaries; REMO context combined with skin-snip microscopy.

column5: Harmonisation: This dataset merges and harmonises records previously distributed across Major-Dataset.csv subsets (formerly 1.1, 3.1 and 6.1). It contains the most complete set of identifiers and variables required for epidemiological analyses (e.g., health zone/health area, and where available age/sex and village). Use this dataset as the primary source for comparative analyses between skin-snip microscopy and anti-Ov16. Recommended use: HA/HZ-level analyses; comparisons of skin-snip and Ov16; most descriptive epidemiology. For GIS mapping, use Dataset 2.1 (clean spatial join keys; fewer missing geocoding fields). Dataset 2.1 includes fewer tested individuals than 1.1 (e.g., 66/173 skin-snip positive in 2.1 vs 74/203 in 1.1). Dataset 2.2 provides additional age/sex information in some strata and contains 2015 REMO observations for individuals not tested by skin snip or Ov16. Dataset 2.2 contains no Ov16, so it cannot be used for Ov16–skin-snip concordance analyses.

column5: Harmonisation: This dataset merges and harmonises records previously distributed across Major-Dataset.csv subsets (formerly 1.1, 3.1 and 6.1). It contains the most complete set of identifiers and variables required for epidemiological analyses (e.g., health zone/health area, and where available age/sex and village). Use this dataset as the primary source for comparative analyses between skin-snip microscopy and anti-Ov16. Recommended use: HA/HZ-level analyses; comparisons of skin-snip and Ov16; most descriptive epidemiology. For GIS mapping, use Dataset 2.1 (clean spatial join keys; fewer missing geocoding fields). Dataset 2.1 includes fewer tested individuals than 1.1 (e.g., 66/173 skin-snip positive in 2.1 vs 74/203 in 1.1). Dataset 2.2 provides additional age/sex information in some strata and contains 2015 REMO observations for individuals not tested by skin snip or Ov16. Dataset 2.2 contains no Ov16, so it cannot be used for Ov16–skin-snip concordance analyses.

column5: Harmonisation: This dataset merges and harmonises records previously distributed across Major-Dataset.csv subsets (formerly 1.1, 3.1 and 6.1). It contains the most complete set of identifiers and variables required for epidemiological analyses (e.g., health zone/health area, and where available age/sex and village). Use this dataset as the primary source for comparative analyses between skin-snip microscopy and anti-Ov16. Recommended use: HA/HZ-level analyses; comparisons of skin-snip and Ov16; most descriptive epidemiology. For GIS mapping, use Dataset 2.1 (clean spatial join keys; fewer missing geocoding fields). Dataset 2.1 includes fewer tested individuals than 1.1 (e.g., 66/173 skin-snip positive in 2.1 vs 74/203 in 1.1). Dataset 2.2 provides additional age/sex information in some strata and contains 2015 REMO observations for individuals not tested by skin snip or Ov16. Dataset 2.2 contains no Ov16, so it cannot be used for Ov16–skin-snip concordance analyses.

column5: Harmonisation: This dataset merges and harmonises records previously distributed across Major-Dataset.csv subsets (formerly 1.1, 3.1 and 6.1). It contains the most complete set of identifiers and variables required for epidemiological analyses (e.g., health zone/health area, and where available age/sex and village). Use this dataset as the primary source for comparative analyses between skin-snip microscopy and anti-Ov16. Recommended use: HA/HZ-level analyses; comparisons of skin-snip and Ov16; most descriptive epidemiology. For GIS mapping, use Dataset 2.1 (clean spatial join keys; fewer missing geocoding fields). Dataset 2.1 includes fewer tested individuals than 1.1 (e.g., 66/173 skin-snip positive in 2.1 vs 74/203 in 1.1). Dataset 2.2 provides additional age/sex information in some strata and contains 2015 REMO observations for individuals not tested by skin snip or Ov16. Dataset 2.2 contains no Ov16, so it cannot be used for Ov16–skin-snip concordance analyses.

column5:
Contains REMO classifications and skin-snip results aligned to health areas/health zones for mapping and spatial summaries. Skin-snip data overlap with Dataset 1.1 but with differences in inclusion criteria and geographic coverage.

Relationship to Dataset 1.1: Dataset 1.1 is a harmonised analytic dataset that includes anti-Ov16 results (enabling test comparisons) and applies stricter inclusion/exclusion of certain villages/records. Dataset 2.1 retains a broader set of REMO/skin-snip records for spatial representation and includes CDTI coverage information for Rethy sourced from the MDA coverage dataset (2014–2015).

Recommended use: GIS/spatial summaries; REMO context combined with skin-snip microscopy.

It contains the most complete set of identifiers and variables required for epidemiological analyses (e.g., health zone/health area, and where available age/sex and village). Use this dataset as the primary source for comparative analyses between skin-snip microscopy and anti-Ov16. Recommended use: HA/HZ-level analyses; comparisons of skin-snip and Ov16; most descriptive epidemiology. For GIS mapping, use Dataset 2.1 (clean spatial join keys; fewer missing geocoding fields). Dataset 2.1 includes fewer tested individuals than 1.1 (e.g., 66/173 skin-snip positive in 2.1 vs 74/203 in 1.1). Dataset 2.2 provides additional age/sex information in some strata and contains 2015 REMO observations for individuals not tested by skin snip or Ov16. Dataset 2.2 contains no Ov16, so it cannot be used for Ov16–skin-snip concordance analyses.

PLoS Negl Trop Dis. 2019 Jul 17;13(7):e0007300. doi: 10.1371/journal.pntd.0007300. PMID: 31314757; PMCID: PMC6663032.". This data also feeded the clinical trials "Single versus Multiple Dose Ivermectin Regimen in Onchocerciasis-Infected Persons with Epilepsy Treated with Phenobarbital: A Randomized Clinical Trial in the Democratic Republic of Congo" AND "Ivermectin as an adjuvant to anti-epileptic treatment in persons with onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy: A randomized proof-of-concept clinical trial"
column3: Yes, fully, with the publications, except for SubsetsPeople_mfloadsÂ… in Logo where there is 3 or 4 more participants and village level info. A subset of this cohort (about 90 out of 400 participants) has also been published on the study "Ivermectin as an adjuvant to anti-epileptic treatment in persons with onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy: A randomized proof-of-concept clinical trial". The data is all the same, but as a trial, it has the number of seizures at 4 different time points after treatment with ivermectin (we also have from the other dataset the baseline).
column5:
Epilepsy-linked dataset with parasitology/serology and partial REMO fields (limited village resolution).
Includes epilepsy variables plus skin-snip, anti-Ov16, and partial REMO fields. Village identifiers are incomplete (village-level detail is available for Draju only; other records are only assignable to Logo HZ, covering Draju, Kanga, Tedheja, Ulyeko and Wala).

Recommended use: epilepsy-linked analyses where village-level resolution is not required (except Draju).

column5: Harmonisation: This dataset merges and harmonises records previously distributed across Major-Dataset.csv subsets (formerly 1.1, 3.1 and 6.1). It contains the most complete set of identifiers and variables required for epidemiological analyses (e.g., health zone/health area, and where available age/sex and village). Use this dataset as the primary source for comparative analyses between skin-snip microscopy and anti-Ov16. Recommended use: HA/HZ-level analyses; comparisons of skin-snip and Ov16; most descriptive epidemiology. For GIS mapping, use Dataset 2.1 (clean spatial join keys; fewer missing geocoding fields). Dataset 2.1 includes fewer tested individuals than 1.1 (e.g., 66/173 skin-snip positive in 2.1 vs 74/203 in 1.1). Dataset 2.2 provides additional age/sex information in some strata and contains 2015 REMO observations for individuals not tested by skin snip or Ov16. Dataset 2.2 contains no Ov16, so it cannot be used for Ov16–skin-snip concordance analyses.

column5:
Contains REMO classifications and skin-snip results aligned to health areas/health zones for mapping and spatial summaries. Skin-snip data overlap with Dataset 1.1 but with differences in inclusion criteria and geographic coverage.

Relationship to Dataset 1.1: Dataset 1.1 is a harmonised analytic dataset that includes anti-Ov16 results (enabling test comparisons) and applies stricter inclusion/exclusion of certain villages/records. Dataset 2.1 retains a broader set of REMO/skin-snip records for spatial representation and includes CDTI coverage information for Rethy sourced from the MDA coverage dataset (2014–2015).

This data also feeded the clinical trials "Single versus Multiple Dose Ivermectin Regimen in Onchocerciasis-Infected Persons with Epilepsy Treated with Phenobarbital: A Randomized Clinical Trial in the Democratic Republic of Congo" AND "Ivermectin as an adjuvant to anti-epileptic treatment in persons with onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy: A randomized proof-of-concept clinical trial"
column3: Yes, fully, with the publications, except for SubsetsPeople_mfloadsÂ… in Logo where there is 3 or 4 more participants and village level info. A subset of this cohort (about 90 out of 400 participants) has also been published on the study "Ivermectin as an adjuvant to anti-epileptic treatment in persons with onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy: A randomized proof-of-concept clinical trial". The data is all the same, but as a trial, it has the number of seizures at 4 different time points after treatment with ivermectin (we also have from the other dataset the baseline).
column5:
Epilepsy-linked dataset with parasitology/serology and partial REMO fields (limited village resolution).
Includes epilepsy variables plus skin-snip, anti-Ov16, and partial REMO fields. Village identifiers are incomplete (village-level detail is available for Draju only; other records are only assignable to Logo HZ, covering Draju, Kanga, Tedheja, Ulyeko and Wala).

Recommended use: epilepsy-linked analyses where village-level resolution is not required (except Draju).

This data also feeded the clinical trials "Single versus Multiple Dose Ivermectin Regimen in Onchocerciasis-Infected Persons with Epilepsy Treated with Phenobarbital: A Randomized Clinical Trial in the Democratic Republic of Congo" AND "Ivermectin as an adjuvant to anti-epileptic treatment in persons with onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy: A randomized proof-of-concept clinical trial"
column3: Yes, fully, with the publications, except for SubsetsPeople_mfloadsÂ… in Logo where there is 3 or 4 more participants and village level info. A subset of this cohort (about 90 out of 400 participants) has also been published on the study "Ivermectin as an adjuvant to anti-epileptic treatment in persons with onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy: A randomized proof-of-concept clinical trial". The data is all the same, but as a trial, it has the number of seizures at 4 different time points after treatment with ivermectin (we also have from the other dataset the baseline).
column5:
Epilepsy-linked dataset with parasitology/serology and partial REMO fields (limited village resolution).
Includes epilepsy variables plus skin-snip, anti-Ov16, and partial REMO fields. Village identifiers are incomplete (village-level detail is available for Draju only; other records are only assignable to Logo HZ, covering Draju, Kanga, Tedheja, Ulyeko and Wala).

Recommended use: epilepsy-linked analyses where village-level resolution is not required (except Draju).

column5: Harmonisation: This dataset merges and harmonises records previously distributed across Major-Dataset.csv subsets (formerly 1.1, 3.1 and 6.1). It contains the most complete set of identifiers and variables required for epidemiological analyses (e.g., health zone/health area, and where available age/sex and village). Use this dataset as the primary source for comparative analyses between skin-snip microscopy and anti-Ov16. Recommended use: HA/HZ-level analyses; comparisons of skin-snip and Ov16; most descriptive epidemiology. For GIS mapping, use Dataset 2.1 (clean spatial join keys; fewer missing geocoding fields). Dataset 2.1 includes fewer tested individuals than 1.1 (e.g., 66/173 skin-snip positive in 2.1 vs 74/203 in 1.1). Dataset 2.2 provides additional age/sex information in some strata and contains 2015 REMO observations for individuals not tested by skin snip or Ov16. Dataset 2.2 contains no Ov16, so it cannot be used for Ov16–skin-snip concordance analyses.

PLoS Negl Trop Dis. 2019 Jul 17;13(7):e0007300. doi: 10.1371/journal.pntd.0007300. PMID: 31314757; PMCID: PMC6663032.". This data also feeded the clinical trials "Single versus Multiple Dose Ivermectin Regimen in Onchocerciasis-Infected Persons with Epilepsy Treated with Phenobarbital: A Randomized Clinical Trial in the Democratic Republic of Congo" AND "Ivermectin as an adjuvant to anti-epileptic treatment in persons with onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy: A randomized proof-of-concept clinical trial"
column3: Yes, fully, with the publications, except for SubsetsPeople_mfloadsÂ… in Logo where there is 3 or 4 more participants and village level info. A subset of this cohort (about 90 out of 400 participants) has also been published on the study "Ivermectin as an adjuvant to anti-epileptic treatment in persons with onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy: A randomized proof-of-concept clinical trial". The data is all the same, but as a trial, it has the number of seizures at 4 different time points after treatment with ivermectin (we also have from the other dataset the baseline).
column5:
Epilepsy-linked dataset with parasitology/serology and partial REMO fields (limited village resolution).
Includes epilepsy variables plus skin-snip, anti-Ov16, and partial REMO fields. Village identifiers are incomplete (village-level detail is available for Draju only; other records are only assignable to Logo HZ, covering Draju, Kanga, Tedheja, Ulyeko and Wala).

Recommended use: epilepsy-linked analyses where village-level resolution is not required (except Draju).

column3: Yes, fully, with the publications, except for SubsetsPeople_mfloadsÂ… in Logo where there is 3 or 4 more participants and village level info. A subset of this cohort (about 90 out of 400 participants) has also been published on the study "Ivermectin as an adjuvant to anti-epileptic treatment in persons with onchocerciasis-associated epilepsy: A randomized proof-of-concept clinical trial". column5:
Contains REMO classifications and skin-snip results aligned to health areas/health zones for mapping and spatial summaries. Skin-snip data overlap with Dataset 1.1 but with differences in inclusion criteria and geographic coverage.

Relationship to Dataset 1.1: Dataset 1.1 is a harmonised analytic dataset that includes anti-Ov16 results (enabling test comparisons) and applies stricter inclusion/exclusion of certain villages/records. Dataset 2.1 retains a broader set of REMO/skin-snip records for spatial representation and includes CDTI coverage information for Rethy sourced from the MDA coverage dataset (2014–2015).

Recommended use: GIS/spatial summaries; REMO context combined with skin-snip microscopy.
